case_title: Sadakat Kotwar and Anr. v. The State of Jharkhand
evidence_type: Eyewitness (two injured eyewitnesses), medical (injury reports), other prosecution witness testimony
aggravating_circumstances: Deadly weapon (dagger) used; grievous stab injuries near chest and stomach, a vital part of the body; accused pushed the victim's husband out of the house before the stabbing
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC s.307 r/w s.34; sentence not stated in the judgment
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction under s.307 r/w s.34 upheld
offence_finally_established: Attempt to murder under IPC s.307 r/w s.34
neutral_facts: The prosecution case is that two accused persons pushed the victim's husband out of a house. Thereafter, the first accused stabbed the victim with a dagger in the ribs, and the second accused stabbed another injured person with a dagger on the right side of the stomach and on the left ribs. The prosecution examined ten witnesses. Two of them were the injured persons, who both supported the prosecution account. Other prosecution witnesses gave consistent statements. The medical evidence recorded an incised wound of about one inch by one inch, muscle deep with haematoma, on the left side of the other injured person's chest in the fourth and fifth intercostal space. It also recorded an incised wound of about one inch by half an inch, pleura deep, in the eighth intercostal space of the left half of the victim's chest. Both injuries were described as caused by a sharp cutting instrument. No sudden quarrel was alleged, and the blows did not appear to have been struck in the heat of the moment.
physical_harm: Two injured persons with grievous incised stab wounds to the chest and stomach/left ribs; no death
premeditation_planning: Not found; court noted no sudden quarrel or heat of the moment, and inferred intention from the weapon, body part and injury
key_evidence_accepted: Testimony of injured eyewitnesses PW7 and PW8; consistent testimony of PW1, PW2, PW4 and PW10; injury descriptions on the medical record
witness_credibility: Injured eyewitnesses PW7 and PW8 found credible; no reason to doubt; other witnesses consistent
trial_duration: offence: not given; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 01.07.2019; Supreme Court: 12.11.2021
legal_representation: Accused: Shree Prakash Sinha, Ms. Mohua Sinha, Rakesh Mishra, Nawalendra Kumar, Shekhar Kumar (Advs.). State: Arunabh Chowdhury, AAG, with Ms. Barnali Chowdhury, Ms. Pragya Baghel, Shantanu Sagar, Vishnu Sharma, Abhishek Roy (Advs.)
investigation_status: Trial completed with 10 prosecution witnesses; FIR and charge sheet dates not stated
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.307 r/w s.34 IPC. High Court: appeal dismissed, conviction upheld (01.07.2019). Supreme Court: appeal dismissed (12.11.2021)
defence_argument: The offence at most falls under s.323 IPC because it was a single blow/injury, not attempt to murder
legal_principle_applied: Intention inferred from weapon, body part chosen and nature of injury; a single blow on a vital part can support s.307 conviction; injured eyewitness evidence has great evidentiary value
precedent_relied_upon: State of M.P. v. Mansingh (2003) 10 SCC 414 (relied on); Mahesh Balmiki v. State of M.P. (2000) 1 SCC 319 (referred to); Jai Narain Mishra v. State of Bihar (1971) 3 SCC 762 (held inapplicable)
judicial_aggravating_factors: Use of deadly weapon (dagger); grievous injuries on vital parts (chest and stomach); no sudden quarrel or heat of the moment
